newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: European feeds calmed by volatile Chicago.
newsitem.headline: European feeds calmed by volatile Chicago.

text.p: European meals and feeds traders once again neglected South American soymeal as potential gyrations on the fund-driven Chicago market kept them sidelined.

Traders said the recent moves in Chicago soycomplex futures had many to loose faith in the market and consumers to believe prices would be coming back down soon. Talk of good-sized South American crops was now being countered by market speculation of flooding hampering the U.S. harvest.
"There are those who want to sow the seeds of panic in the market and although the weather could yet play a factor, this is the sort of talk we have heard before," one trader said.
But another trader said he would not be surprised to see the Chicago market back up to around $9 a bushel at some point this month. "It depends on what the funds make of it," he said.

Chicago opened mixed with nearbys lower but the more distant new crop months up on the the U.S. planting concerns. Traders there cited weather forecasts for a wet spring and predcictions of melting snow leading to flooding in the Midwest.
Traders in Europe were sceptical of the move. "The market can change direction so fast at moment, I want put any store by how it looks at the European close," one trader said.
